rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 6 compounds if possible and map the elution window without risking truncation. The wide phi range and mid-length gradient should reveal whether retention is concentrated early, late, or across the whole window.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to cut t_last below 10 min while keeping every peak inside the gradient. The first and last peaks correspond roughly to phi_e about 0.25 and 0.43 in the scout, so a narrower, steeper window centered on the observed elution region should greatly shorten the run without sacrificing resolution.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so this run probes whether the gradient can be shortened further while maintaining all adjacent pairs above 1.5. Keeping the same phi window isolates the effect of slope and may identify a faster equally optimal method.

Resolution margins remain very large, so shorten the gradient again to find the speed limit at the same selectivity. This keeps the successful window fixed and tests whether an even faster fully resolved method is possible.

The worst pair is still comfortably above 1.5 at tG 4 min, so test the minimum allowed gradient time on the same window. This should reveal whether the method can be pushed to the fastest possible run while retaining full resolution.

At 2 min the only failing pair is the first one, indicating the front of the gradient is too weak for the earliest peaks. Raising phi0 one step while keeping the fast 2 min program should move those early peaks later and may recover their spacing without sacrificing the very short run.

The 2 min method is close to full resolution and the limiting pair is still the first one, so raise phi0 another step to further tune the early selectivity while preserving the shortest runtime. This targets the only unresolved pair with minimal disturbance to the rest of the chromatogram.

Changing phi0 did not fully recover the first-pair resolution at 2 min, suggesting that pair is more sensitive to selectivity than to gradient-window placement. Lowering temperature one step may increase retention and modestly alter selectivity enough to push the critical pair above 1.5 while keeping the very fast 2 min gradient.

Now that lower temperature restored full resolution at 2 min, test whether a slightly higher phi0 can recover a bit of speed without losing the critical first-pair margin. This keeps the fastest successful tG and productive temperature while refining the front-end window.

The 2 min, 35 C method has room on the critical first pair, so raise phi0 one more step to see if the run can be nudged slightly faster while preserving full resolution. This continues optimizing the front end of the shortest successful gradient.

Phi0 = 0.25 at 35 C was fully resolved, and increasing phi0 to 0.30 hurt the first pair, so keep the better front-end condition and instead raise phi1 one step to see whether the last peak can be pulled slightly earlier without affecting the critical early pair much. This is a targeted speed optimization of the shortest successful method.

The last peak dropped substantially when phi1 was raised to 0.75 while maintaining full resolution, so test one more increase in phi1 to see if the run can be shortened further. The limiting pair is still the first one, and it remained above 1.5, so there is some room to probe a slightly stronger final solvent.

At phi1 = 0.80 the method is very fast but the first pair is right at the 1.5 threshold, so lower phi0 one step to give that critical pair a bit more breathing room while keeping the stronger final solvent and 2 min gradient. This should preserve the short t_last with a safer resolution margin.

The best fast condition so far is phi0 0.25, phi1 0.80, tG 2, T 35, with the first pair exactly at the threshold; since lowering phi0 made that pair worse, keep phi0 at 0.25 and test a stronger phi1 to see if the last peak can be shortened further while monitoring whether the critical pair remains acceptable. This directly probes the final lever left for a still faster fully resolved method.

Increasing phi1 beyond 0.80 makes the critical first pair fall below 1.5, so step back to the successful phi1 = 0.75 condition and lower temperature one more step to see whether added selectivity can support even stronger retention margins for the front pair. This checks whether 30 C opens room for a still faster high-phi1 variant afterward.

At 30 C the critical first pair gained substantial margin at phi1 = 0.75, so now retest phi1 = 0.80 to see if that extra selectivity allows a faster method than the 35 C version while keeping full resolution. This is the most promising next step to improve speed without changing the already optimal 2 min gradient.

Lowering temperature to 30 C improved the critical first-pair margin, so retest phi1 = 0.85 under these conditions to see whether the previously too-aggressive high-phi1 method can now achieve full resolution with an even shorter t_last. This is the most direct route to a faster optimal method.

The 30 C run at phi1 = 0.85 remains fully resolved with useful margin on the first pair, so test phi1 = 0.90 to see whether the final peak can be pulled even earlier while staying above the 1.5 resolution threshold. This is the next logical speed optimization on the best-performing 2 min method.

Phi1 = 0.90 at 30 C is still fully resolved with a small but real margin on the critical first pair, so test the strongest allowed final solvent to see whether the run can be shortened further. This is the final straightforward speed probe on the current best 2 min setup.

Phi1 = 0.90 at 30 C is the fastest fully resolved run so far, and phi1 = 0.95 showed the first pair is just over the edge, so test a slightly lower phi0 with the successful phi1 = 0.90 to see whether the front pair gains selectivity while retaining nearly the same short t_last. This is a local refinement around the current best speed point.

The current best speed point is phi0 0.25, phi1 0.90, tG 2, T 30, and moving phi0 downward hurt the critical first pair, so probe one step upward to confirm whether 0.25 is the local optimum for front-end selectivity at this high phi1. This is a final local check around the fastest fully resolved condition.

Raising phi0 to 0.30 at phi1 = 0.90 improved the critical first pair while keeping the run very short, so now combine that better front-end selectivity with phi1 = 0.95 to test whether the faster high-phi1 method can also remain fully resolved. This is the most promising remaining route to the shortest optimal method.

The current fastest fully resolved method is phi0 0.30, phi1 0.95, tG 2, T 30, and the limiting first pair still has comfortable margin, so raise phi0 one more step to see if the run can be shortened slightly further without dropping below R = 1.5. This is the most direct remaining local optimization around the best point found.

Phi0 = 0.35 was too aggressive, so return to the fastest fully resolved setting at phi0 0.30, phi1 0.95 and lower temperature one step to see whether extra selectivity margin is gained without much loss of speed. This final check tests whether the best method can be made more robust while staying essentially as fast.

At 25 C the critical first pair has substantially more margin, while the only clear failure was phi0 0.35 with the stronger phi1 0.95; stepping phi1 back to 0.90 may let phi0 0.35 run fully resolved and potentially shave a little more time. This is the last high-value edge test around the current fastest robust region.
